paragraphs: Fluvie is a Flutter package that turns widget code into real video files. You build a video the way you build a screen, with Scenes and the Flutter widgets you already know, you say how long each thing lasts, and Fluvie renders every frame and encodes it into an MP4 (or a GIF, or an image sequence) with FFmpeg. No video editor, no manual timeline, no After Effects.

Think of it as a tiny film studio that already speaks Flutter: you direct, Fluvie handles continuity, and FFmpeg runs the projector. No timeline to scrub, no keyframe spreadsheet, no 2am debugging because frame 412 is one pixel off.
features: Declarative. Compose Scenes and elements like any Flutter screen.
Cacheable. The frame cache keys on content, so caching, golden tests, and batch rendering just work.
Headless. Render from the CLI, an HTTP API, or an MCP server. No display needed.
Conversational. Describe a video in plain language; a model writes editable Fluvie code (or a spec) and renders it.
